status_note: Draft generated from the attached Excel curriculum and current official documentation. Requires editorial review, version-specific verification, and practical execution in a supported Excel environment before publication.

content.intro: This lesson covers Office Scripts Fundamentals as part of Office Scripts and Power Automate. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Office Scripts Fundamentals contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: Office Scripts and Power Automate require a supported Microsoft 365 environment and tenant configuration. Do not assume a desktop macro or a browser-hosted script will be available on every account.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Office Scripts Fundamentals focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: TypeScript-based script syntax; Workbook and worksheet access; Ranges, values, and formatting; Basic control flow and functions. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: Sets cell A1 on the active worksheet to Report ready. This is an illustrative Office Script; availability and tenant policy must be checked.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use the Office Scripts editor in a supported Microsoft 365 environment. Validate workbook/sheet assumptions first; this snippet is not run by the CodeLeaf lesson page.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for office scripts fundamentals. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates office scripts fundamentals. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates office scripts fundamentals; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency. For a complete curriculum practice scenario, also complete “Office Scripts Workflow” using the synthetic dataset `assets/data/practical-23-office-scripts-workflow.csv`; see the linked additional exercise file.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Sets cell A1 on the active worksheet to Report ready. This is an illustrative Office Script; availability and tenant policy must be checked.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Office Scripts Fundamentals supports the workflow in Office Scripts and Power Automate.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
